topic: Certified exact optimization at bounded canonical-response width for multi-intervention quasi-Markovian SCMs. Fix a finite acyclic quasi-Markovian SCM with observed alphabets at most q, a compatible positive rational observational table, and a treatment touching at least three C-components. The input fully expands every canonical response-mass coordinate, raw observational equality, nonnegativity constraint, and interventional-query monomial, together with a nice decomposition of the scalar response-factor primal graph of width k; B is this full binary input length. Prove that a fixed external-parent context partitions each response block into at most q^2 equality-support cliques, so it has at most q^2(k+1) coordinates. Split disconnected equality systems, prove the resulting compact rational product and block-affinity, and compute exact sharp endpoints by complete support enumeration and standard max-sum/min-sum elimination in 2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)} poly(B) bit operations. Return finite rational compatible SCMs attaining both endpoints and independently checkable support, separator-table, and backpointer certificates. For binary at-most-two-child components and ell explicitly relevant original response blocks, also prove the B^{O(ell(1+log B)^2)} exact algorithm without a width assumption. Credit Shridharan–Iyengar for the canonical multilinear reduction, Dechter for bucket elimination, Duarte et al. and Zaffalon et al. for general causal/credal bounds, and causaloptim-lean for existing linear certificate formalization. The CRAN causaloptim graph-to-bound workflow is the prospective same-question consumer: this theorem supplies a certified fallback for small higher-degree queries, not a claimed implementation. Exclude hardness, implicit response columns, statistical projection, new elimination machinery, and benchmark gains. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fresh presolve independently derived the raw equality-clique bound, compact equality-component factorization, width-preserving contraction, exhaustive rational support criterion, denominator bit bound, and binary logarithmic-square rank bound. Exact rational checks reproduced 8,192 canonical tuples, 4,096 cubic monomials, 64 positive observed cells, and sharp endpoints 11/64 and 53/64 in a legal three-component chain; they additionally enumerated 80 and 32 vertices in the later disconnected factors and 243 projected tuples. An interleaved-parent example showed why the component kernel is 1/4 where the ordinary conditional is 3/8. Destructive checks covered omitted normalization, singular supports, zero endpoint masses, running intersection, irrelevant blocks, degree versus relevant-block count, and live collisions; generic elimination and existing canonical-validity results are explicitly credited. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove executable refinement: acceptance by the serialized certificate verifier must imply universal compatible-SCM interval validity and rational endpoint realization for every well-formed canonical input, with generator completeness and the stated bit bound. EARLY KILL TEST: Run the verifier on the cubic, interleaved-parent, disconnected-equality, singular-support, and zero-mass cases, then delete a necessary vertex and corrupt a separator entry; stop if an incorrect endpoint or source-kernel mismatch is accepted, and pivot if repair changes the representation contract. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_multiintervention_width_bounds.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does explicit canonical-response optimization for a positive rational quasi-Markovian SCM admit exact sharp multi-intervention bounds in 2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)} poly(B) bit operations when supplied with a width-k scalar response-factor decomposition?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Shridharan–Iyengar identify the relevant C-component degree but provide only local optimization in the degree-at-least-three regime, while credal-network hardness prevents importing a generic low-treewidth inference result. The prior relational run further proves that an assignment-materializing checker can require exponentially many records even when its target graph has treewidth zero. The missing bridge is a structural theorem for the explicitly expanded scalar response program: external-parent contexts must yield at most q^2 equality-support cliques per response block, equality contraction must preserve the supplied width, and finite support enumeration must produce exact rational separator messages without reconstructing the doubly exponential canonical state space.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graph-native sharp-bounds theorem proving the clique and width-preservation lemmas, an exact 2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)} poly(B) rational elimination algorithm, and finite compatible rational SCMs attaining both endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: Its transition from one or two intervened C-components to the unresolved higher-degree regime supplies the closest motivation and problem-formulation arc.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent confounding prevents point identification -> quasi-Markovian factorization gives a multilinear sharp-bounds program -> three or more intervened C-components create a globally difficult objective -> bounded scalar response-factor width may recover exact tractability

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the C-component factorization, objective-degree reduction, and product-vertex optimality proof, replacing Frank-Wolfe search with complete local support enumeration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its feasible region is already a Cartesian product of component polytopes and its objective is block-affine, which is the algebra required before width-bounded elimination.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt bucket elimination's induced-width separator invariant and its maximizing or minimizing backpointer reconstruction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After support choices become finite, the endpoint computation is a max-sum or min-sum graphical-model problem; the new step is proving that canonical equality processing preserves its width.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the equivalence between discrete causal bounding and polynomial optimization, including explicit observational compatibility constraints and endpoint sharpness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the semantic bridge from feasible response masses to compatible causal data-generating processes that exact elimination must preserve.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing causal optimizers establish semantic equivalence to linear or polynomial programs and supply symbolic, numerical, or approximate solvers, but the scan found no certificate language joining canonical-input parsing, exhaustive support accounting, separator recurrences, endpoint backpointers, and finite-SCM reconstruction. The earlier certificate theorem is univariate and starts from a dense polynomial plus exhaustive incidence. A bounded-width multivariate verifier must additionally reject omitted vertices, locally consistent but globally incompatible separator tables, singular equality supports, zero endpoint masses, and source-kernel mismatches. The proof bottleneck is a refinement invariant showing that exact serialized arithmetic reconstructs one compatible SCM and dominates every other compatible SCM.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A soundness-and-completeness refinement theorem for an executable Boolean verifier, including parser well-formedness, local-support and separator invariants, universal endpoint dominance, rational SCM reconstruction, generator completeness, and a polynomial or FPT certificate-size bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its user-facing path from a declared causal graph and query to guaranteed bounds is the closest framing for a certificate-carrying exact fallback.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal assumptions produce analytically intractable identified sets -> automatic compilation yields a polynomial program -> numerical optimization supplies progressively valid bounds -> exact rational instances require portable certificates whose replay establishes sharpness and realization

method_exemplars.technique: Formalize bucket elimination by an induction equating every separator-table entry with the optimum over eliminated variables, then use stored backpointers to reconstruct a global optimizer.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Separator tables and backpointers are precisely the finite objects needed to certify global endpoint dominance after response-support enumeration.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate untrusted certificate generation from skeptical exact-arithmetic replay and prove that checker acceptance implies the underlying algebraic claim.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired causal verifier has the same producer-checker architecture, with support and separator consistency replacing scalar root certificates.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit response-function matrices and primal-dual vertex geometry to turn feasibility, objective evaluation, and local optimality into replayable rational equalities and inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a certificate-shaped linear core that the new theorem must compose through a higher-degree elimination trace.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest canonical-compression result treats single-intervention linear programs and still identifies double-exponential response cardinality as the obstacle. Query-aware pruning likewise leaves the higher-degree regime heuristic. The missing step is combinatorial: for at-most-two-child binary components, one must prove a logarithmic-square rank or support bound for each explicitly represented relevant equality block and show that enumerating only the ell query-relevant original blocks remains complete even when the global response primal graph has unbounded width.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A parameterized exact-algorithm theorem proving a B^{O(ell(1+log B)^2)} exhaustive rational-support procedure, completeness of the enumerated supports for both sharp endpoints, and an explicit reconstruction of attaining finite SCMs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its canonical-state-explosion narrative followed by input-aware compression is the closest setup for the stronger relevant-block parameterization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Canonical SCMs yield exact partial-identification programs -> response-mechanism cardinality can be doubly exponential -> observational equalities and query structure allow compression for one intervention -> sparse-child multi-intervention queries require an exact ell-parameterized support theorem

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt valid-hyperarc pruning by aggregating partial response assignments that are indistinguishable to the observational constraints and causal query.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both approaches avoid full canonical-function enumeration; the new proof must replace LP-specific pruning with a rank-controlled support enumeration valid for degree at least three.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse canonical partitions and response-function equality matrices, then apply rational-polytope support and vertex arguments inside each enumerated block.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired algorithm uses the same response-mass coordinates but must bound the support patterns relevant when the objective couples ell blocks.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing credal reductions and quasi-Markovian programs prove separability across exogenous roots or C-components, but do not state the finer within-block factorization required here. Prior work also warns that replacing independent latent-root factors by one unrestricted response simplex creates false endpoints. The missing proof must derive normalizations for each equality-incidence component from the positive observational table, preserve singular and zero-mass faces, show that every expanded query monomial remains affine in each factor, prove width-preserving contraction, and glue selected rational factor vertices into one shared deterministic-mechanism, independent-root SCM.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff rational factorization-and-gluing theorem proving a compact product isomorphism, block-affinity of every expanded query monomial, width-preserving contraction, bounded-denominator finite-SCM decoding, and checkable rejection of nongluable supports.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates exact causal bounds through observationally constrained local credal sets and makes compact representability the central computational issue.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unknown exogenous distributions partially identify causal queries -> observations impose linear restrictions on response masses -> compact local credal representations permit exact inference -> disconnected equality support may yield a finer exact product representation

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the exact correspondence between observational compatibility constraints and local credal sets, including reconstruction of SCM distributions from feasible credal parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed result refines the same semantic map from one response block into several equality-connected rational factors.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the component-wise-affinity and product-extreme-point proof to the finer equality-incidence decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once exact factorization is established, this machinery connects compact local factors to global sharp endpoint attainment.

method_exemplars.technique: Use response-function equality matrices and finite-polytope vertex characterizations to construct rational local supports and witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its linear response-mass representation is the natural substrate for proving that the incidence split is a genuine polyhedral product rather than a relaxation.

literature_map:
Shridharan–Iyengar (ICML 2023) reduce multilinear degree to the number of intervened C-components, but switch to a stationary-point heuristic at degree at least three.
Shridharan–Iyengar (ICML 2022) show query-aware hyperarc pruning and exact LP computation for a special class, establishing response-state compression as viable.
Duarte et al. (JASA 2023) prove that general discrete causal bounds are polynomial-program optima and use spatial branch-and-bound with guaranteed outer and epsilon-sharp bounds.
Zaffalon–Antonucci–Cabañas (PGM 2020) give an exact SCM-to-credal-network map, compact only for a characterized subclass, and identify scalability as the limiting issue.
Zaffalon et al. (IJAR 2024, arXiv:2307.08304) retain exact credal bounds for a subclass, prove NP-hardness even on polytrees, and otherwise emphasize approximate causal EM.
Mauá et al. (JAIR 2014) show that strong credal inference is NP-hard even on tree structures, so ordinary network treewidth cannot explain the proposed tractability.
Dechter (Artificial Intelligence 1999) gives exact max/sum bucket elimination with complexity exponential in induced width, supplying the separator invariant and backpointer machinery.
Chen–Darwiche (UAI 2022) refine treewidth for Bayesian inference with deterministic mechanisms but do not optimize over compatible exogenous credal sets.
Arroyo et al. (UAI CAR 2025, arXiv:2509.03548) expose doubly exponential canonical cardinality and obtain polynomial-cardinality column generation only for single-intervention linear programs.
Sachs et al. (JCGS 2023, arXiv:2003.10702) provide canonical response-function matrices and tight symbolic vertex bounds for a linear class; broader nonlinear settings lack their tightness guarantee.
Jonzon–Sachs–Gabriel (R Journal 2023, arXiv:2209.03657) provide the causaloptim graph-to-symbolic-bound workflow, making it a downstream consumer rather than prior coverage of higher-degree exact optimization.
Huber et al. (TPM 2023, arXiv:2310.03352) compile repeated counterfactual evaluations into symbolic arithmetic circuits but accelerate an EM inner approximation rather than certify global endpoints.
The scan found no paper joining explicit canonical coordinates, scalar response-factor treewidth, complete rational support enumeration, and independently replayable separator/backpointer certificates for multi-intervention sharp SCM bounds.
